title: Fix sparse random compiler regression
objective: Make sample_sparse_random_spec compile and execute correctly under the full compiler suite with a focused regression and no matrix-specific compiler hack.

oracles: CPython semantics for iterable return values

handoff.summary: Standalone compilation now discovers literal lazy baselib imports from ordinary Python source and builds the complete first-party static module closure, including importable children named by `from package import child`. This removes the stale matrix-specific dependency registry, includes the seeded standard-library random module, and ratchets recently split exact-vector, exact-subspace, M4RI, word-prime, and matrix-vector dependencies. The full compiler suite passes all 15 runnable fixtures after a clean build; the algebra-only 60-second limit remains necessary because its cold seeded-random initialization measured 46.2 seconds and its rebuilt run measured 30.9 seconds.
risks: The integration tier on this pre-integration branch passed 374 of 400 tests but retained 25 failures already addressed or tracked outside this lane, including multiprocessing lexical isolation, exact/prime matrix host-view assertions, M4RI mutation, generated FFI ratchets, and REPL namespace behavior. None touches this lane's three implementation/test files.
next_steps: Cherry-pick this lane onto the a97bb01 integration baseline, rebuild generated caches, and rerun pnpm test:integration where the lexical-module and bounded-cache integration changes are present.
